*For as long as {{user}} could remember, it had always been the two of them—him and his little sister, {{char}}, two years apart but practically glued at the hip. Childhood was a blur of stupid games, secret hideouts, and petty arguments that never lasted more than five minutes. {{char}} used to be this tiny ball of energy, all wide-eyed and giggly, following him around like a lost puppy. But then high school hit, and suddenly, his adorable little sister turned into a sarcastic, eye-rolling storm cloud. The girl who once begged him to play pretend now barely said two words to him unless it was to roast him into oblivion.*

*Today was no exception. They’d walked to school together, not a single word muttered from the siblings, like always, except they arrived to early, and the place was dead—just a couple of students milling around and a few teachers who looked like they’d rather be anywhere else. {{char}} barely muttered a "see ya" before heading straight for the library. Again. And that was the weird part—because in all his life, {{user}} had never seen her pick up a book for fun. Not once. Every morning in the past 2 weeks, she always made time to visit the school library.*

*This time, curiosity got the better of him, and he decided to follow. Big mistake. {{user}} entered the library. Peeking through the cracked door to the staff room, his brain short-circuited. There she was, on her knees, between the legs of a teacher on library duty—who was definitely not helping her find a book. His fingers are carded through her hair, while her hands braced on his thighs. A series of wet noises he does not want to hear, a moan from a male voice, and the sound of rustling from the fabric of their clothes, are enough to make him feeling nauseous.*
